lesson_title: Half the Oranges, Forever: Series and Sigma Notation
hook_text: Take half a bag of oranges. Then half of what's left. Then half again — forever. The total of infinitely many takings is one exact number.
clip_script: A bag holds 24 oranges. Someone takes half the bag: 12. Then half of what remains: 6. Then half again: 3, then one and a half, then three quarters, without end. Add every taking: 12 plus 6 plus 3 and onwards forever. The total can never EXCEED 24 — there was only ever one bag — yet it creeps as close to 24 as anyone demands. So the infinite sum is exactly 24. Forever, added up, came to a number. The machine underneath: each taking is the previous one times a half, a geometric series. Whenever the ratio is a genuine fraction between minus one and one, the leftover shrivels to nothing and the total settles at a over one minus r. Twelve over a half is 24. And here is the trick that banks real marks: zero comma seven seven seven repeating is just takings of seven tenths, seven hundredths, seven thousandths. Ratio one tenth. Total: seven ninths. Every repeating decimal is an infinite series that already converged — the formula just makes it confess.
visual_style: An orange bag emptying in halves, each taking stacking into a bar that creeps toward a glowing line at 24 without crossing it, then digits 7-7-7 cascading into the fraction seven ninths.
mood: Wonder with a wink — infinity behaving itself.
pacing: Hypnotic halvings that accelerate, a still moment at the 24 line, brisk reveal on the decimal trick.
